problemStatement.formal: Classify regular polytopes by Schlaefli-symbol determinant tests: six regular 4-polytopes, three regular 5-polytopes, and stabilization to the simplex, hypercube, and cross-polytope families from dimension 5 onward.
problemStatement.plain: Formalizes the higher-dimensional regular-polytope story around the exceptional four-dimensional cases. The proof counts the six regular 4-polytopes, rules the exceptional symbols out in dimension 5, and records the high-dimensional stabilization pattern.
whyMatters: Dimension 4 is the exceptional case where the 24-cell, 120-cell, and 600-cell appear alongside the infinite families.
Schlaefli determinant checks give a compact algebraic route to the classification.
The metadata makes a large completed proof discoverable through its classification theorems rather than an empty placeholder.

proven: `valid4D_count` proves there are exactly six valid regular 4-polytope Schlaefli triples in the modeled candidate set.
`regular_4polytope_classification` packages the 4D candidate, positivity, and exclusion checks.
`regular_5polytope_classification` proves the three regular 5-polytope families in the modeled setting.
`stabilization_from_5D` records the persistence of the three infinite families and the failure of the exceptional 4D cases beyond dimension 4.
open: A deeper Coxeter-group or incidence-geometry treatment would be a separate extension beyond this computable determinant classification.
knownResults.goal: Backfill searchable metadata for the completed regular-polytope classification proof.

currentState.focus: Built full 4D classification with Schläfli determinant in Z[sqrt(5)]
currentState.nextAction: Fast path: Quick Mathlib search, then directly to ACT if obvious approach found.

builtItems: QSqrt5 exact arithmetic ring for Schläfli determinant computation
schlaefliDet4/5/6: computable Coxeter-Schläfli determinants at each dimension
Polytope4Data structure with Euler characteristic verification for all 6 4D polytopes
RegularFamily inductive type for the 3 infinite families
insights: The Schläfli determinant sin²(π/p)·sin²(π/r) - cos²(π/q) reduces to Z[√5] arithmetic
Same symbols fail in 5D: det = 64-32√5 < 0 since 4096 < 5120
{4,3,...,3,4} always has det = 0 (Euclidean cubic honeycomb) — proved by recurrence
All-3s sequence det = (n+1)/2^n — always positive, decaying geometrically
The 24-cell {3,4,3} is unique: only regular polytope existing in exactly one dimension
Dimension 4 is the golden dimension: 6 polytopes > 5 in dim 3 > 3 in dim ≥ 5
nextSteps: Build with Docker to verify compilation
Connect to Coxeter group theory for deeper algebraic treatment
Prove the closed-form det = (n+1)/2^n for all-3s Schläfli symbols inductively
